en: Salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa.
O dear one, one should employ rites of subjugation and attraction during the spring;
in summer, the rite of causing enmity should be performed, and likewise, the rite of immobilization during the rainy season.
Killing is prescribed for the winter season, while pacifying rites are traditionally taught for autumn.
In the winter season, one who is skilled in the seasonal rites should perform the rite for prosperity.
Spring is indeed said to be in the forenoon, summer at midday;
the rainy season is in the afternoon, and the dewy season is remembered to be at twilight.
At midnight during the autumn season, the mantra for the heating of the cauldron is recited.
O Sage, all that you have spoken regarding the seasons and their respective order— || 4 ||
Therefore, those who are deficient in that [truth] do not succeed, even though they exert themselves with effort.
For there is no other cause; they certainly perish, and not otherwise. || 5 ||
Thus concludes the determination of the seasons.
Now follows the determination of the lunar days (tithis).
O wise one, one should perform rites of subjugation on the seventh lunar day.
On the thirteenth day of the third [fortnight], one should indeed perform the rite of plowing.
One should perform the rite of eradication on the second lunar day, and likewise, one should purify on the eighth.
And immobilization (staṃbhanam) [is performed] on the fourteenth day, the fourth, and also on the first.
One should employ the Mohana [mudrā] on the ninth and likewise on the eighth [lunar day].
Killing is auspicious on the twelfth lunar day, and likewise on the eleventh.
On the fifth and the full moon day, one should perform the rites beginning with the *dvāntika*.
The lunar days (tithis) have been declared in sequence for the sake of accomplishing all vidyās. || 9 ||
Thus it is said.
Now follows the determination of the lunar mansions (nakṣatra).
It effects paralyzing, deluding, and the most excellent subjugation.
The Māhendra and Vāruṇī [offerings] should also be performed here, as they grant success. || 10 ||
One should perform the rite of inciting enmity (*vidveṣa*) and the rite of expulsion (*uccāṭana*) through the conjunction of the fire and wind [mantras].
[The appropriate asterisms are] Jyeṣṭhā, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Anurādhā, Ārdrā, and Rohiṇī. (11)
The Māhendra-maṇḍala is said to grant the accomplishment of one's activities;
it consists of Uttarabhādrapadā, Mūlā, and likewise Śatabhiṣā. || 12 ||
Pūrvabhādrapadā and Āśleṣā are to be known as situated in the middle of the waters;
Pūrvāṣāḍhā is likewise remembered as that which, when combined, bestows success upon the rite. (13)
Svāti, Hastā, Mṛgaśirā, Citrā, Uttara-phalgunī, Puṣyā, and Punarvasu are proclaimed to be situated within the circle of fire (vahni-maṇḍala). || 14 ||
Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, Citrā, Svāti, Abhijit, and Maghā are the [nakṣatras] for śramaṇas.
Viśākhā, Kṛttikā, Pūrvaphalgunī, and likewise Revatī. || 15 ||
Standing in the center of the Varuṇa-maṇḍala, she is renowned for her true deeds.
Thus it is said.
Now follows the determination of the thumb and so forth.
In rites for pacification, for nourishment, and likewise in rites of sorcery. || 16 ||
The wise one should place [the fingers] beginning with the index finger (tarjanī) upon [the mudrā] in their proper sequence.
Likewise, when mounted upon the thumb, it accomplishes all rites, whether auspicious or otherwise. || 17 ||
Thus it is said.
Now follows the determination of medicinal herbs.
When combined with ritual procedures and mantras, even a harsh remedy becomes fruitful.
But that which is devoid of ritual and mantra shall become like a mere wooden image.
But at the edge stands the mountain Śubhāra, which possesses the medicine that removes dullness.
The accomplishment of his purpose will come to pass, for there indeed exists a seed of power.
Now follows the procedure for taking the medicinal herbs from the trees at the Valmika well.
Having first gone to the foot of a tree, he should join [the two ends] after they have been consecrated with mantras.
Having offered guggulu incense and medicinal herbs at the boundary of the field, one should recite the mantra while holding the hand of the woman who dwells there. Mantra:
Oṃ! May the vetālas, piśācas, rākṣasas, and sarīsṛpas all depart; they are to be driven away by the chanting of the Vṛkṣoda-śivā hymns.
Having recited the mantra, he joined his palms and offered prostrations with his hands folded.
Now, the mantra for the three layers of the cloth.
Oṃ! Homage to you, O you who have arisen from death, who increase strength and virility!

Grant me strength and long life; do not harm me through sin. He who digs you with the *brahman*-mantra, he who digs you with the *bhṛgu*-mantra—he approaches you with that [power] which belongs to Indra and Varuṇa; with that [power], him you [approach].
I shall explain the mantra with my own hand; when it has been cast down by the power of the Uṣapāta, let there be no loss of its splendor.
Remain right here for kalpas and become the accomplisher of my task. Once my task is accomplished and perfected, you shall go to heaven.
Now, listen to the mantra.
Oṃ hrīṃ caṇḍa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. This mantra [should be recited] on a Sunday, or under the Puṣya nakṣatra, or on a Sunday coinciding with the Puṣya constellation.
Then indeed, he recited the mantra with distress.
Oṃ hrīṃ phaṭ svāhā. Now, the mantra for the one who pays homage:
Oṃ baladaṇḍa mahādaṇḍa svāhā | khatrīyāla mālinī svāhā || One should recite each [mantra] seven times.

Oṃ aṃ reṃ toṃ vaṃ tiṃ reṃ roṃ daṃ iṃ kāṃ gaṃ yoṃ goṃ ḍaṃ taṃ yoṃ cāṃ pāṃ paṃ siṃ ciṃ riṃ gāṃ ḍaiṃ paṃ siṃ phoṃ riṃ gāṃ ḍaṃ īśvara Mahādeva Kivācā Gaurī Pārvatī Kivācā choṃ daṃ vaṃ hiṃ rāṃ choṃ daṃ (2) hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Now, the Karuṇa mantra: Oṃ karuṇa phate avarutrarale phaṭ svāhā. Thus.

Oṃ! O Goddess, by the command of the divine Guru, this is the command. The *thoma* mantra, the *nanyākhana*, the *senakalasā*, the *thoma* mantra, the *vonesena*, the *kuhma*, the *phekatuye*, the *maphasyaṃdaṅāvaconi*, and the *ca*.
Oṃ! O Indrajāla, excellent mantra, Muru Mahāvarī Devī!
Oṃ! [Protect me from] thieves, elephants, tigers, and snakes; grant success through the command of the Guru.
By means of this dhāraṇī-mantra,
one will undoubtedly attain the state of a Buddha.
Oṃ akāsayoginī oṃ hūṃ mahā ājñā hūṃ phaṭ. Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times;
it will not fail to cause the [target] to tremble and fall from the tree branch.

Oṃ satye sā chigva kuladhyā pādhochāra pādhochārasi uti āyoparatigayo rhuṃ guru oṃ lelevetapāthi svāhā. This is the mantra for the *dhāra* [seat]. Next is the mantra for the *nama-eva-napya-āsana* [the seat of non-dual entry]. Then follows the mantra for the *senaka-sātha* [the host of attendants], namely: *hākala vakāyāvatha ca pālāhāti sa ketakā ca musyāla*.

Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Now, the seed-mantra of Abhra (cloud): *Abhrabīja*, *Jīmūta*, *Ambuvṛddha*, *Valaṅghana*, and the five seed-mantras beginning with *Vaṃ*; these are the others, not false. *Vīṃ*. Now, the seed-mantra of Ābdhi (ocean): *Ābdhibīja*, as well as *Sindhu*, *Sāgara*, and *Sāgara*.
The four seed-syllables beginning with *rūṃ*, as well as the others, are artificial; *rūṃ*. 2.
Now, the seed-syllable of the eon.
The seed of the eon, the dissolution, the destruction, and the seed of decay.
Kṣāmaka, Kṣuraka, Kṣaudra, and likewise Kalpāntabījaka.
Dhvaṃ, and other seeds, and muṣṇau, and others made of skin. Dhruṃ.
Oṃ kṣiṃ kṣauṃ, delude! Now, by reciting these three mantras three times, one indeed brings about the delusion of people.

*Sana hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* Thus are the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Having assigned the syllables of the mantra to the thumbs and little fingers of both hands, one should assign five syllables each to the feet, waist, heart, face, and head. [The meditation follows.]
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Next, he describes the application of the mantra.

Having extracted the Astra-mantra— consisting of the syllable *dhruvam* (the letter *ha*) with a final stop (*tha*), joined with the Bindu (*m*), and adorned with the right ear (*ra*)— this is remembered as the five-syllabled mantra.
In the Jayāgre rite, victory indeed comes through recitation and not otherwise;
having placed the mantra named Jaya upon the heart and likewise upon the openings of the eyes.
By performing the recitation while touching the heart, one shall conquer enemies at that very moment.
Illumination.
Oṃ daṃ uṃ phaṭ ||1||
Krodhīśa joined with fire (Ra), conjoined with the head of Oṃ;
Pavana joined with fire (Ra), conjoined with the head of Oṃ.
This mantra of two syllables is extremely difficult to find even in the three worlds;
this supreme mantra should be recited by one who does not consume meat or worldly delicacies.
Even an incurable king, along with his sons, friends, and kinsmen,
and whoever else belongs to his entire circle of birth and lineage from every side— [all these perish].
All of them come under one's control through the recitation of this along with the *śrāddha*. [Prakāśa] KROṂ PROṂ || 5001 || 2 ||
Then follows the immobilization of tigers.
Then follow two *māyās*, then *lakṣmī*, and at the end of that, the seed-syllable of light (*jyotirbīja*);
one should then utter the words *hiṃ ehi*. This mantra consists of seventeen syllables.
Having consecrated his lips with this mantra, he should cast [the remainder] in the four directions;
there will be a paralysis of tigers, of this there is no doubt.
Its illumination is: Hrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hiṃ ehi.
Next is the procedure for extracting the *kīla* from mantras.
Having taken a ritual stake (kīlaka) made of lotus wood measuring five finger-breadths in length, the purification should be performed.
The mantra is as follows:

Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hphreṃ hsauṃ haṃsa aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ hūṃ saiṃ saṃ haiṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ saṃ khhphruṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ aṃ kaṃ caṃ ṭaṃ taṃ paṃ yaṃ saṃ! Destroy the previously established *kīlaka* at that place! (2) Grant success to the *kīlaka* performed by me! (2) Bestow the accomplishment of the mantra! (2) Destroy all defects!
(2) Fulfill my desires! O Śrīpūrṇeśvarī! O Śrīviśveśvarī!
Salutations to Śrīgaṇeśa! Then follows the mantra for purifying the tongue.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Next, the Sudarśana mantra.
And with the addition of "tarpayāmi" along with the word "śabda," it becomes preceded by the *praṇava* (Om) and ending with the armor (*varma*) and weapon (*astra*) mantras.

For the Sudarśana mantra: the seer (ṛṣi) is Ahirbudhnya, the meter (chandaḥ) is Anuṣṭubh, the deity (devatā) is Viṣṇu in the form of Sudarśana, the seed-syllable (bīja) is *sāṃ*, and the power (śakti) is *hūṃ*. *Ācakrāya svāhā* | *Vicakrāya svāhā* |
*Sucakrāya svāhā*. *Dhīcakrāya svāhā*. *Saṃcakrāya svāhā*. *Jvālācakrāya svāhā*.

Thus is the mantra of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅgamantra*). Having placed the *praṇava* on the head through the visualization of the three qualities (*guṇatraya*) as the sun and moon, [one places it] in the middle of the brows and the face.
One should place the six syllables beginning with *sa*, colored like fire, by means of meditation upon the heart, the secret place, the knees, and the feet.
Thus is the binding of the directions.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ, I bind with the wheel; obeisance to the Wheel, Svāhā!
In this manner, [one proceeds] to the south-eastern, southern, south-western, western, north-western, northern, and north-eastern [directions].
Having uttered "mūrdhāmadharām" for the feet, I bind the directions with the wheel.

Having performed the binding of the ten directions with the mantra "Namas cakrāya svāhā," and having visualized a wall of fire surrounding oneself with the mantra "Trailokyaṃ rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā," one should perform three breath-retentions (*prāṇāyāma*) according to the root mantra until the cessation [of the breath].
One should meditate upon the form of the Blessed One: May Bhāskara protect us—
he whose entire radiance illuminates all directions, whose eyes are terrifying, whose face is ablaze with flashing loud laughter and blossoming fangs.
Then Hari, bearing a discus, sword, mace, lotus, pestle, conch, noose, and goad in his arms, with tawny hair and wearing a crown, appeared before you.

Having thus reflected and performed the internal worship, one should also worship [the deity] on the external seat (bāhyapīṭha) together with the enclosures (āvaraṇas). Therein, the first enclosure consists of the limbs (aṅgas).
The second [hand] holds the discus, conch, mace, lotus, club, spear, noose, and goad.
The third [mandala] consists of Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Rati, Prīti, Kīrti, Kānti, Tuṣṭi, and Puṣṭi, who are flame-colored and hold two lotuses and joined palms in their hands.
The fourth [mudrā] is with Indra and the others. Here, during the worship, one should display the Cakramudrā with the right hand for the purpose of bringing about the presence of the Blessed One.
We know the Sudarśana; we meditate upon the Great Flame; may that Discus inspire us.

Thus ends the Śūdr̥śana Gāyatrī. At the commencement of rites such as recitation (japa) and fire-offerings (homa), one should recite the Śūdr̥śana Mālā mantra for the sake of all-encompassing protection.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Great Sudarśana, the Great Wheel, the Great Flame, the One of Blazing Form;
protect me from all sides, O One of Great Power! Svāhā! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

For this sixteen-syllable *Sudarśana* garland-mantra (*mālāmantra*), the ritual placement of mantras (*nyāsa*), meditation (*dhyāna*), worship (*pūjā*), and so forth, should be understood in the same manner as for the six-syllable *Sudarśana* mantra.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Then, the five-syllable mantra of Garuḍa.
And that [mantra] consists of the syllables beginning with the letter *kṣa* joined with the third vowel (*u*), preceded by the *praṇava* (*oṃ*) and ending with the word *agnijāyā* (*svāhā*).
Of this mantra, Ananta Rudra is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Paṅkti is the meter (*chandas*), the Lord of Birds (*pakṣīndra*) is the deity (*devatā*),
*Oṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), and *svāhā* is the power (*śakti*).
*Oṃ jvala jvala mahāgati svāhā | Garuḍāya namaḥ svāhā | To Garuḍa, on the head.*
Svāhā! O Garuḍaprabhañjana, (2) Prabhedaṇa, (2) Vinnāsaya, (2) Vimarddaya, (2) svāhā!
O you who assume a fierce form, remover of all poisons, terrify! Burn everything! Reduce it to ashes! Svāhā!
Unobstructed power, unobstructed wisdom.
